questions.stem: A patient performs a maximal forced expiration followed by full inspiration, generating this closed loop of flow versus volume. What test produces this tracing?

explanation.summary: The flow-volume loop is produced during spirometry; the peak of the expiratory limb is the peak expiratory flow and the width of the loop spans the vital capacity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The flow-volume loop is produced during spirometry; the peak of the expiratory limb is the peak expiratory flow and the width of the loop spans the vital capacity.

questions.stem: One flow-volume loop here is shifted toward higher lung volumes with a scooped expiratory limb, while the other is shifted toward lower volumes. Which disease pattern does the loop shifted toward higher (leftward) volumes represent?

explanation.summary: Obstructive disease raises lung volumes from air trapping, shifting the loop left with reduced expiratory flow and a scooped limb; restrictive disease reduces volumes, shifting the loop right.
explanation.whyCorrect: Obstructive disease raises lung volumes from air trapping, shifting the loop left with reduced expiratory flow and a scooped limb; restrictive disease reduces volumes, shifting the loop right.

questions.stem: Among these flow-volume loops from upper airway obstruction, one shows flattening of only the inspiratory limb while the expiratory limb is preserved. Which type of obstruction does that pattern indicate?

explanation.summary: Variable extrathoracic obstruction flattens the inspiratory limb only; variable intrathoracic obstruction flattens the expiratory limb; fixed obstruction flattens both limbs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Variable extrathoracic obstruction flattens the inspiratory limb only; variable intrathoracic obstruction flattens the expiratory limb; fixed obstruction flattens both limbs.

questions.stem: A patient exhales forcefully into the mouthpiece shown while a technician records volume-time and flow-volume tracings. What pulmonary test is being performed?

explanation.summary: The handheld mouthpiece connected to a recording unit that plots volume-time and flow-volume loops is a spirometer. Spirometry measures forced expiratory volumes and flows (e.g., FEV1, FVC) to characterize obstructive versus restrictive patterns.
explanation.whyCorrect: The handheld mouthpiece connected to a recording unit that plots volume-time and flow-volume loops is a spirometer. Spirometry measures forced expiratory volumes and flows (e.g., FEV1, FVC) to characterize obstructive versus restrictive patterns.

questions.stem: This spirometry tracing marks the volume exhaled in the first second and the total forced exhaled volume. A reduced ratio of these two values would most specifically indicate which type of defect?

explanation.summary: The plateau curve shows FEV1 (volume at 1 sec) and FVC (total forced vital capacity). A low FEV1/FVC ratio (<0.7) defines airflow obstruction, as in asthma or COPD; restrictive disease lowers both proportionally and preserves the ratio.
explanation.whyCorrect: The plateau curve shows FEV1 (volume at 1 sec) and FVC (total forced vital capacity). A low FEV1/FVC ratio (<0.7) defines airflow obstruction, as in asthma or COPD; restrictive disease lowers both proportionally and preserves the ratio.
